scenarios.name: a fresh button on the page: Did Mount in the first frame, Enabled true, the three states false, Child Index and Children Count 0, This itself
a click on an unfocused button: Pointer Down, Focused (the browser gives a pressed <button> the keyboard), Pointer Up, Click — Pressed ends the frame where it began
a second click on a focused button: Pointer Down, Pointer Up, Click — the keyboard was already there
Keeps Focus on: a click fires Pointer Down, Pointer Up and Click, and the keyboard stays where it was
a disabled button takes no press, release or click, and no focus — but the pointer still hovers it
a finger lands on a disabled button and lifts: nothing — no Pressed, no Pointer Down or Pointer Up (C64: a finger on a disabled control reports nothing, as Enabled promises)
hover on, press, leave while held: Hover true then false, Pressed true then false — leaving ends the press (Hover End, no Pointer Up)
press and release in one frame: Pressed is unchanged at the frame's end, Pointer Down and Pointer Up both fire
a press held across a frame, then a click: Pressed true in the first frame, false again with the click's own release
the Focus action puts the keyboard on the button (Focused, Done); a second Focus is Done with nothing more; Blur takes it off (Blurred, Done); a Blur with no focus is Done alone
a Focus on a disabled button is Done and nothing is focused — the element is there to ask, and it refuses silently
a Tab onto the button and off it: Focused true with Focused, false with Blurred; a second Tab onto a focused button does nothing
Mounted off with the pointer over it: Will Unmount, and Hover goes with the element — Hover false and Hover End (D30); a click finds nothing; a Focus is Unchanged; Mounted on: Did Mount again

trace.message: Focus arrived while this button was not on the page, so nothing was focused. A Focus is not kept for later: send it once the button has mounted, for example from its Did Mount or its row’s

scenarios.name: Mounted written to its current value changes nothing; a truthy string mounts, 0 unmounts
Enabled follows its input as a boolean and is sent only on a change: 0 disables, 'no' enables, a repeat is silent
disabled while focused and hovered: Enabled false is all that moves; re-enabled, a click fires Pointer Down, Pointer Up and Click with the focus it already holds
Scroll Into View and every look or layout input change nothing on the wire
Enabled off and a Focus in the same frame: the button is still enabled on the page, so it takes the keyboard; in the next frame a Focus is Done and takes nothing
focused, then disabled: Focused stays true — a disabled element gives the keyboard up to nobody, so a Blur is Done and nothing fires, a Tab away does nothing; re-enabled, Blur takes it

a person acts on a painted page: Mounted written off and an act in the same frame find no element (a Focus after it is Unchanged); written on, the act meets the element (a Focus after it is Done) — every act, both ways

Visible off: a hidden button is under no pointer and takes no keyboard — every act raises nothing; the Focus action is Done with nothing; shown again, a click is a click

trace.message: "height" is wired, and the parent stacks its children along that same axis, so the value arrived as a PERCENTAGE (dimension ports default to "%") and became flex-grow 100 — a ratio against the siblings that also grow, not a height. Send a {value, unit} object instead of a bare number, or give this port a px value in the property panel first: a bare number arriving over a wire is merged into the unit the port is already holding.
